factual_claims.claim: TKM Grupp AS reported a challenging but operationally stable 2025, with profitability weakening as consumer demand remained subdued and the Estonian automotive market contracted sharply.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'The year 2025 will go down in history as a year of a challenging economic environment and major challenges for Estonian retailers... Consumer confidence remained low... The introduction of the motor vehicle tax... had a strong impact on the Estonian automotive retail sector.' The Financial Performance section confirms weakened profitability with revenue and profit declines.

factual_claims.claim: Consolidated revenue was 919.6 million euros, down 2.6% from 944.6 million euros in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Performance section states: 'The Group’s audited consolidated sales revenue for 2025 amounted to 919.6 million euros, representing a decrease of 2.6% compared to 2024, when sales revenue totalled 944.6 million euros.'

factual_claims.claim: Gross profit declined to 254.6 million euros from 259.8 million euros, although the gross margin improved slightly to 27.7% from 27.5%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Ratios table shows gross profit of 254.6 million EUR for 2025 vs 259.8 million EUR for 2024. The gross margin improved to 27.7% in 2025 from 27.5% in 2024, as stated in the Financial Performance section.

factual_claims.claim: EBITDA fell 14.7% to 77.4 million euros and the EBITDA margin decreased to 8.4% from 9.6%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Ratios table shows EBITDA of 77.4 million EUR for 2025 (vs 90.7 million EUR for 2024), representing a 14.7% decrease. The EBITDA margin was 8.4% in 2025 vs 9.6% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Operating profit declined 26.6% to 34.9 million euros, reducing the operating margin from 5% to 4%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Ratios table shows operating profit of 35 million EUR for 2025 (rounded from 34.9) vs 48 million EUR for 2024, a 26.6% decline. The operating margin was 4% in 2025 vs 5% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Profit before tax was 24.3 million euros, down 31.4%, while net profit fell 36.1% to 17.5 million euros.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Ratios table shows profit before tax of 24.3 million EUR for 2025 vs 35.5 million EUR for 2024 (31.4% decrease). Net profit was 17.5 million EUR for 2025 vs 27.5 million EUR for 2024 (36.1% decrease).

factual_claims.claim: Net margin decreased to 2% from 3%, and earnings per share fell to 0.43 euros from 0.67 euros.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Ratios table shows net margin of 2% for 2025 vs 3% for 2024. Earnings per share were 0.43 EUR in 2025 vs 0.67 EUR in 2024, as stated in the Share section.

factual_claims.claim: The decline occurred despite a 1.5 million euro reduction in interest costs and a 1.2 million euro decrease in income tax expense.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Performance section states: 'Net profit was positively affected by a decline in interest on the Group’s borrowings, providing relief of 1.5 million euros for the year compared to the previous year. The company’s income tax expense decreased by 1.2 million euros in 2025 due to the recalculation of deferred income tax...'

factual_claims.claim: The 2024 comparative result also included approximately 4.0 million euros of one-off gains related to investment-property revaluation and the sale of two non-core Latvian properties.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Performance section states: 'The comparative base year included one-off profit of 4.0 million euros, of which 2.1 million euros resulted from the revaluation of investment properties and 1.9 million euros from extraordinary profit arising from the sale of two non-core properties in the Group’s real estate segment in Latvia.'

factual_claims.claim: Labour costs increased 3.7%, while other operating expenses rose only 0.2%, reflecting the Group’s cost-control and supply-chain optimisation measures.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'Continuous improvement of work processes and optimisation of the supply chain... have helped to keep labour costs under control. factual_claims.claim: The main pressure came from car trade.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Performance section attributes the revenue decline primarily to the car segment: 'As expected, the Group’s sales revenue was most significantly affected by the substantial decline in the sales revenue of the car segment.'

factual_claims.claim: Segment revenue decreased 11.9% to 176.9 million euros, profit before tax fell 48.5% to 5.7 million euros, and net profit declined 54.4% to 4.3 million euros.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Business Segments table shows car trade revenue of 176.9 million EUR in 2025 vs 200.8 million EUR in 2024 (11.9% decrease). factual_claims.claim: Estonia’s new passenger-car market fell 48.6%, affected by the introduction of the motor vehicle tax and weaker consumer confidence, although stronger markets in Latvia and Lithuania partly offset the decline.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Economic Environment section states: 'The motor vehicle tax that entered into force in Estonia from 2025 has had a significant impact... At the same time, sales of new passenger cars increased by 31.4% in Latvia and by 39.3% in Lithuania.'

factual_claims.claim: Supermarket revenue increased 0.3% to 611.9 million euros, but net profit fell 38.6% to 9.5 million euros amid lower sales volumes, greater promotional activity and costs associated with the Jõgeva Selver refurbishment.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Business Segments table shows supermarket revenue of 611.9 million EUR in 2025 vs 610.4 million EUR in 2024 (0.3% increase). Net profit was 9.5 million EUR in 2025 vs 15.5 million EUR in 2024 (38.6% decrease). The Management Report attributes this to 'lower sales volumes... greater promotional activity... and one-off additional costs' from the Jõgeva Selver refurbishment.

factual_claims.claim: Department-store revenue decreased 1.1% to 103.0 million euros and the segment recorded a 0.5 million euro loss.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Business Segments table shows department store revenue of 103.0 million EUR in 2025 vs 104.2 million EUR in 2024 (1.1% decrease). The segment reported a loss before tax of 0.5 million EUR in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Real-estate revenue increased 5.1% to 7.7 million euros, while net profit rose 20.5% to 6.3 million euros, supported by rental income and lower borrowing costs.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Business Segments table shows real estate revenue of 7.7 million EUR in 2025 vs 7.3 million EUR in 2024 (5.1% increase). Net profit was 6.3 million EUR in 2025 vs 5.2 million EUR in 2024 (20.5% increase). The Management Report cites 'rental income from the logistics centre... and lower borrowing costs' as drivers.

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash flow remained substantial at 65.6 million euros, compared with 73.1 million euros in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Consolidated Cash Flow Statement shows operating cash flows of 65,613 thousand EUR (65.6 million) in 2025 vs 73,064 thousand EUR (73.1 million) in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Total investment decreased to 25.5 million euros from 36.6 million euros, while year-end cash fell to 29.5 million euros from 45.5 million euros.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Investments section states: 'The Group’s total investments in 2025 amounted to 25.5 million euros (36.6 million euros in 2024).' The Cash and Cash Equivalents note shows 29,516 thousand EUR (29.5 million) in 2025 vs 45,454 thousand EUR (45.5 million) in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Working capital was negative at 14.2 million euros, mainly because 32.1 million euros of loans maturing in 2026 were classified as current liabilities; refinancing had begun and management reported no liquidity issues.

The loans maturing in 2026 are planned to be refinanced during 2026. In the management’s assessment, the company does not face liquidity issues.'

factual_claims.claim: The Group opened new KIA and Škoda facilities in Lithuania and a new dealership in Peetri, Estonia, and continued store and digital-system upgrades.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The 2025 Overview section lists: 'A new KIA showroom was opened in Tallinn, and KIA and Škoda sales showrooms were opened in Vilnius... The Group continued to develop its information systems, investing in upgrades to both e-shops and business software.'

factual_claims.claim: In January 2026, it agreed to acquire Škoda-related businesses in Tallinn and Harju County, subject to completion conditions.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Event after the reporting period section states: 'Group’s subsidiary TKM Auto OÜ will, subject to the fulfilment of the conditions precedent to final completion of the transaction, acquire a 100% interest in three companies engaged in the retail sale and servicing of vehicles: Rohe Auto AS and SKO Motors OÜ...
